title: Renewed Consolidation Called For Malaysia Shares
text:
Renewed Consolidation Called For Malaysia Shares January 03, 2019, 06:32:00 PM EDT By RTTNews Shutterstock photo
( RTTNews.com ) - The Malaysia stock market on Thursday ended the two-day slide in which it had fallen almost 30 points or 1.9 percent. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now rests just above the 1,675-point plateau although it figures to head south again on Friday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is broadly negative, with bad news from Apple expected to weigh heavily on technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were firmly in the red and the Asian bourses are expected to follow suit.
The KLCI finished modestly higher on Thursday as gains from the plantations and telecoms were capped by weakness from the financial sector.
For the day, the index picked up 7.72 points or 0.46 percent to finish at 1,675.83 after trading between 1,666.22 and 1,680.78. Volume was 1.7 billion shares worth 1.1 billion ringgit. There were 367 decliners and 366 gainers.
Among the actives, Press Metal plummeted 4.24 percent, while Tenaga Nasional surged 2.38 percent, Genting Malaysia soared 2.03 percent, IOI Corporation spiked 1.36 percent, Axiata Group jumped 1.33 percent, Petronas Chemicals climbed 0.87 percent, Digi.com advanced 0.68 percent, Genting skidded 0.67 percent, RHB Capital collected 0.38 percent, PPB Group perked 0.35 percent, Dialog Group dropped 0.33 percent, Maybank shed 0.32 percent, Public Bank lost 0.24 percent and Kuala Lumpur Kepong, IHH Healthcare, CIMB Group, Sime Darby and Petronas Gas all were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is brutal as stocks opened sharply lower on Thursday and remained that way throughout the session.
The Dow shed 660.02 points or 2.83 percent to 22,686.22, while the NASDAQ lost 202.43 points or 3.04 percent to 6,463.50 and the S&P fell 62.14 points or 2.48 percent to 2,447.89.
Downwardly revised guidance from Apple (AAPL) contributed to the early selloff on Wall Street, with the tech giant plunging 10 percent. The lower guidance was attributed to a greater than expected impact from economic weakness in some emerging markets and China.
In economic news, the Institute for Supply Management noted a bigger than expected slowdown in U.S. manufacturing activity in December. Also, payroll processor ADP reported much stronger than expected U.S. private sector job growth in December.
Crude oil prices extended gains to a fourth successive session Thursday on hopes the proposed reduction in oil output by OPEC will allay fears of excess supply in the market. Crude oil futures for February ended up $0.55 or 1.2 percent at $47.09 a barrel.
Closer to home, Malaysia will release November numbers for imports, exports and trade balance later today. In October, imports were worth 80.1 billion ringgit and exports were at 96.4 billion ringgit for a trade surplus of 16.3 billion ringgit.
